notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-b at head 0397dec: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, uncommitted false, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the only "Skill" text is the tool definition) or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests.

Rules changed since db91c23 (git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's rules only Chain fallible steps with `with` changed. It is graded against the current text, where the verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and the new sentence "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." All three violating blocks have exactly that shape: opus-1's apply_discount/2 (line 53), sonnet-1's total/2 (line 76) and sonnet-2's apply_code/2 (line 44, the keyword form `with {:ok, parsed} <- parse_code(code), do: ...`, which is the shape of the example SKILL.md showed before this change). A run with no `with` is "not exercised", as in the previous sweep's grades and this sweep's skill grade. The other rules that changed (the new do: rule, the captures rule, and Assert with patterns in testing.md) are not in this case's list; I found no break of the new do: rule (opus-1's `def apply_discount(%__MODULE__{}, code) when is_binary(code),` / `do: {:error, :discount_already_applied}` at lines 58-59 is a head that mix format wrapped, which the rule allows).

`with`, violating runs out of five: one-step `with` 3 of 5 (opus-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2); `else` 0 of 5; a `case` nested in a `with` body 0 of 5. Sonnet-1 also handles apply_code/2's single fallible call with case (lines 59-62), which the rule asks for, but its total/2 has the one-step `with`. The Haiku runs write no `with`: they test membership with `if normalized in @discount_codes` and call no fallible helper. In the previous sweep 1 of 5 baseline runs broke the rule (sonnet-1); opus-1 there used case, and sonnet-2 used function clauses.

Unchanged rules graded to the previous sweep's standard: Update structs, Convert external strings to atoms, Return {:ok, value} or {:error, reason}, Store and compute money, Naming, Before you finish. A total function that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc treats a priced SKU as the caller's job: opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 name the KeyError; haiku-2's @doc (lines 64-66) only states the precondition ("`prices` maps each SKU in the cart to its price in cents."), which I also counted as clean. Map.put/3 or Map.delete/2 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the struct-update pattern the rule forbids. Naming: role names normalized, sum, acc, parsed and discounted are held to the earlier standard, which passed them. Sonnet-1 uses a bare `_` in four places (line 38 `%{^sku => _}`, line 83 `defp parse_code(_)`, line 95 `defp discounted(subtotal, _)`, line 98 `defp shipping(_)`); the previous sweep passed bare `_` catch-alls in the same functions written as case clauses (its baseline-opus-1 and baseline-sonnet-2), so they are not counted here. A stricter reading of "Give ignored values a descriptive name with a leading underscore ... when it tells the reader what is being ignored" would turn sonnet-1, and Sonnet, to violated.

Before you finish: 4 of 5 violated, with one judgment call matching this sweep's skill grade. Opus-1 ran `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8; mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -4` after its last edit but no separate mix compile; the mix test output shown begins "Compiling 1 file (.ex)\nGenerated shop app" within the 8-line tail, so the app compiled with no warning. Step 2 says "Compile, and fix every warning ... Use `mix compile` in a Mix project." This grade calls it clean, as the skill grade did for its sonnet-1 in the same position; the literal reading would turn Opus to violated. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 ran only mix test and mix format --check-formatted (never the formatter, mix compile or Credo); both Sonnet runs ran only mix format && mix test (never mix credo --strict), as in the previous sweep.

Refused commands (only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc were pre-approved): haiku-1 an exploratory xargs sh -c listing, and `mix format --check-formatted 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "exit=$?"`, re-run as plain mix format --check-formatted; haiku-2 a $(find ...) cat loop, a `which mix elixir; (...)` chain and a `mix format --check-formatted; echo ...; mix test` chain, re-run as separate mix test and format-check commands; opus-1 a cat > lib/shop/cart.ex heredoc, after which it used Write; sonnet-1 an xargs ls listing and a python3 heredoc edit (it carried no mix command), after which it used Write and Edit; sonnet-2 an xargs ls listing, and one call to a non-existent tool named bash (input "true"), which failed as an unknown tool, not a permission refusal. No refused command carried mix compile or mix credo, so the Before you finish verdicts stand.

Verified in scratch copies of each project (copied without _build and deps, then mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five (14, 16, 13, 14 and 13 tests). A probe run with mix run gave: 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five (sonnet-1 returns {:ok, cents}); opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 reject a second code, both Haiku runs replace it; removing 5 of 2 units empties the items and removing 1 of 2 leaves 1; BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five; " save10 " is accepted by both Haiku runs (trim and upcase) and rejected by the other three (sonnet-1 trims but is case-sensitive); an unpriced SKU raises KeyError except in sonnet-1, which returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, "APPLE"}}. Rounding of the SAVE10 discount: opus-1 and sonnet-2 halves up, the Haiku runs and sonnet-1 down.

other_violations follows the previous grades: sums written with Enum.reduce where Enum.sum_by/2 fits are listed under the Enum/Map rule (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2; sonnet-1 halts on a missing price with reduce_while, which sum_by cannot do), and multi-step pipelines written on one line are listed under the pipeline rule. Not listed: pipelines that start with Cart.new(), because the project's own test file starts its pipelines that way (SKILL.md, "Existing projects"); @doc without ## Examples, because the project's existing @docs have none; sonnet-2's two one-condition `if ..., do: ..., else:` lines in total_price/2 (lines 66-67), which the branching rule allows ("Use `if` for a single boolean condition"); haiku-2's comment at line 89, which states the rounding choice.
Expected reads (testing.md when the run adds or changes tests) applies to skill runs. All five baseline runs added tests and read no skill file, as the baseline prompt requires.
